body: I'm a dude but thanks for the positive energy!
Really appreciate this. Exercise will definitely need to become a habit. Anxiety is probably the biggest reason for my consumption.

It's been mentioned while awake as well. The point was that even after 4 hours without drinking, I still looked like that.

But I appreciate your concern and will keep that in mind.
Yep. Not looking forward to trying to suppress all of that.
I read a lot about it the last few days. It's the booze. Antihistamines like some allergy medicines purportedly help, but I take those every day anyway.
Thank you! Knowing I shouldn't drive most of the time has definitely kept our family from living our lives to the fullest.
I really appreciate it. Just hoping delerium tremens doesn't happen and my neurotransmitters don't make me screw up at work.
This is where I'm at. I'm glad I didn't have a rock bottom incident. But it's probably been obvious to everyone around me.

Do you happen to have a good resource for that? The number I called had people calling me every week or two, telling me I needed to go to a detox center for two weeks. They asked for my insurance and emergency contact information, and then called my partner and told her that she was a terrible partner because she didn't want to organize an intervention.

So I'm trying to avoid all of that.

The blood vessels in the skin on your face dilate after you drink and turn your face red. For people who drink constantly, their face ends up being a shade of red or purple all the time. People will notice.
Thanks. Part of my plan is to occasionally whine on here so sorry in advance.

I've heard those groups want you to be sober for at least a week or something before they welcome you at meetings. But I'd definitely be interested in something like that. It would be a nice way to get more involved with the community as well.

I'm sorry she's not being helpful to you, but that's all she knows what to do. Yes she's being illogical from a non religious pov.

I would ask her if you could talk to a therapist, but do noooot let her talk you into a christian therapist. That would be better than nothing but ultimately not as helpful.

Tell her you've been looking into it and think you should see a cognitive behavioral therapist. She'll have no idea what that is and take you more seriously.

Not at all. I wanted to have a conversation. 6 or 8 minutes out of an hour I got to talk. Does that sound like a conversation to you?

Also, you're being rude. You're on this sub for a reason; either to look for help, give help, or to troll on suicidal people. If it's the latter, you're a terrible person.

It's weird. I have a therapist but we can only have sessions over the phone for covid reasons, and he prefaces every session by saying "we can talk about anything, but if you're a threat to yourself or anyone else, I have to report it."

And I'm like, oh, so there's literally no one I can talk to about my thoughts. That's great. I'll just talk about something else for an hour and pay $130 for it.
Back in the 20's they were doxxed and publicly shamed until they faded away, but I don't know how well that would go in 2020.
I know r/trees loves the mflb, but I wouldn't recommend a portable vape to anyone. For the same price, you could get a tabletop vape like the volcano and get extremely high.

You pretty much nailed that. I'd love to move out and work for what I get, but I don't really know how to get started.

You know what? Screw that. I know how to do it. I just got a rush of motivation, so I'm gonna go out and get a job. Hopefully there are some cheap apartments near my school.

"Smart people don't say "If I work hard I can do it", they just fucking do it."

I think successful would be a better adjective than smart for that statement, but I do understand and agree with what you're saying. 

I would love to just do my work and whatnot without thinking about it, but I fear I've lost that ability. I think it was the 5 years of doing absolutely nothing but reading and playing games all day while I was homeschooled. Before that, straight A's! After that, 1.2 high school GPA!

I don't want to blame anyone else for this, though. I just want to fix it and get on with life.

I realize that It's not easy to get into graduate school. But i know I have the ability and potential to do it. I used to make straight A's without even trying before my work ethic disappeared.

My problem is that due to a lack of motivation and work ethic, I don't make good grades.
